Hi Lena — thanks again for the product demo earlier today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can map an appropriate hosting + migration path for Acme: 

Key context I captured from the call:
- You need PHI-capable inference for clinical triage (FHIR payloads) — data residency in us-east required.
- Current usage: 200k tokens/day, peak 60 concurrent requests; latency target 250ms P95 for short responses.
- Two existing model sources: (1) calls to a third-party hosted API (HyperScale AI) and (2) an internal self-hosted cluster (older nvidia A100 fleet) used for nightly batch jobs.

Clarifying questions (helps us recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):
1) Is data allowed to leave Acme’s VPC? If not, Private (VPC) or on-prem is likely required.
2) Do you need customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and SSO (SAML/SCIM)?
3) Any blackout windows for cutover (e.g., weekend-only maintenance)?
4) Are you planning to retire the self-hosted cluster or keep it as a fallback during migration?

Next steps I propose:
- Camila to provide a short tech note on VPC peering, KMS support, and model compatibility (we have a suggested lift-and-shift path).
- I’ll share a draft SoW and a migration checklist for your infra/security review.
- 30-minute follow-up next week to review constraints and pick a target hosting mode.

Attachments: redwood-sow-draft.pdf (draft SoW), migration-checklist.csv (initial checklist) — both attached for context.

Thanks,

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: must remain within our AWS account in us-east-1. We cannot have PHI routed through public multi-tenant endpoints.
- Keys/SSO: yes to both. We require customer-managed KMS and SAML for SSO; SCIM would be nice but not mandatory at launch.
- Cutover: prefer a staged migration during weekend maintenance windows; initial canary to run in parallel for 2 weeks.
- Self-hosted cluster: we plan to decommission the old A100 fleet within 6 months but want it available as a safety net during transition.

We also have a security questionnaire (attached) that our InfoSec team will use to evaluate deployment options — please have your security lead return answers inline.

Regarding hosting preference: our preliminary leaning is Dedicated or Private VPC. Cost aside, isolation + KMS are must-haves. Can you outline the incremental operational overhead for Private vs Dedicated? For example, who manages OS and kernel patches, network egress rules, and SLA scope?

Appreciate it — happy to join the follow-up next Wednesday.

Best,
Lena Morales
VP, Engineering Ops | Acme Health

Hi Lena — Camila from Solutions here, following up with technical specifics that will help choose between Dedicated and Private VPC. Answers below are purpose-built for the PHI/US-residency constraint you mentioned.

1) Isolation & key management:
- Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated): single-tenant GPU pools managed by Redwood; network egress is restricted by account-level policies. We can offer customer-managed KMS integration and SSO (SAML + SCIM). OS-level patching is handled by Redwood for the Dedicated control plane; you get node-level maintenance windows and a change log.
- Private (VPC/private deployment): control plane can be customer-hosted in your VPC; you retain full control over network ACLs, subnets, and KMS; Redwood provides an ops bundle for day-2 tasks but OS/kernel patching is typically delegated to your infra team. This reduces our ability to push emergency patches without your approval but increases isolation.

2) Migration approach (compatibility & risk):
- For traffic now routed to HyperScale API: we recommend a DNS-level gradual reroute with weighted routing and a model-compatibility shim to normalize differences in tokenization or response schema.
- For self-hosted A100 cluster: suggested path is data + model export -> validate locally on a small Dedicated pool -> run parallel canary traffic (1–2% traffic) against Redwood Dedicated before cutting to Private if you choose that.

Technical constraints / questions for you:
- Do you need persistent KV-cache across restarts? We have optional KV persistence for long-running sessions but it affects storage configuration.
- Which model formats are you using for the self-hosted cluster (PT, ONNX, Triton bundles)? We need this to validate quantization support and kernel compatibility.

I’ll attach a short tech note and a migration checklist for your infra team. Happy to run a 45 min deep dive with your infra folks next week.

Camila Reyes

Thanks Camila — that helps. Quick answers inline: 
- KV-cache: yes, persistent KV across short restarts is important for our triage flows.
- Model formats: mostly PT + a few Triton bundles; we also run a nightly conversion job to ONNX for batched workloads.

We’ll have our infra lead join the deep dive. I’ve also attached the security questionnaire. Please have your InfoSec/engineering leads return answers some inline comments by EOD next Monday so we can keep timelines moving.

Also, to your question on operational overhead: if Private means our team has to own kernel/OS patching, that will increase our headcount/time commitments. We’re open to Dedicated if Redwood can provide stricter patch windows and clear escalation SLAs.

Lena
